transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE); Jamie Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Rao (Nimbus, Sr. Infra Eng); Marcus Lee (Nimbus, CTO); Samir Patel (Nimbus SRE)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Covered current networking blockers (NAT, firewall rules, VPC peering), routing for private subnets, upcoming kernel/GPU driver upgrade required for latest runtime, and plan for throughput benchmarks (8k seq). Agreed next steps: share diagrams, run NAT egress test in scheduled window, SE to run bench and provide results, schedule maintenance window for driver upgrade.

Topics:
- Networking: peering, route tables, NACLs, firewall/iptables
- Routing: egress, NAT, private endpoints
- Upgrades: kernel/GPU driver and Redwood runtime upgrade path
- Benchmarks: sequence length tests, KV cache effects, batching
- Security: audit logs, KMS, SSO (SAML), compliance artifacts

Action items (short): see action_items field above

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick check in — same agenda as last week: network blockers, bench plan, and the driver upgrade. Priya, you okay to kick off with any updates on the infra side?

[00:22] Priya (Nimbus): Yeah hi, thanks. So we did the first round of VPC pairing — sorry, peering — with the test account; routes mostly propagated but we saw some egress dropping when traffic hits the NAT instance. Samir's been digging in. We still have a couple of denied flows in the firewall logs.

[00:55] Samir (Nimbus SRE): Yep, to add, the NAT is a t3.medium right now so it's not ideal but for the test we wanted to emulate a constrained egress. We're seeing high conntrack usage and some timeouts. I'll attach logs.

[01:30] Jamie (Redwood SE): Okay that makes sense. On our side the runtime will retry a few times but repeated timeouts look like connection resets which triggers fallbacks and hurts throughput. If you can open the NAT for 10.8.0.0/16 outbound during a short window we can do an aggressive bench to see the delta.

[02:10] Marcus (CTO): Quick question — are there any firewall rules that Redwood requires inbound? We want to keep everything locked down.

[02:35] Alex: No inbound public endpoints for Redwood Private; communications flow outbound from your VPC to the private control plane or via peering depending on how you set it up. We'll put a list of IPs and ports in the diagram. We'll also provide iptables examples if you prefer host-level rules.

[03:05] Priya: Awesome. Also we saw some odd log entries where "KV cache" gets transcribed as K-V cash — you know how the agent names get funky — but the point is we want to test with KV cache on and off because our workload is chatty.

[03:40] Jamie: Good call. We'll run the bench both ways — KV on and KV off. I'll include metrics for latency p50/p95 and tail latency and token throughput.

[04:15] Alex: And we'll surface model version differences. There was a runtime tweak in the latest build that improves attention kernel selection for long sequences, but it requires a GPU driver minimum. That's the kernel/driver upgrade we mentioned.

[04:45] Marcus: What's the risk of that upgrade? Downtime? Data loss?

[05:05] Jamie: It's low risk but it is a maintenance window. For a single node it's about 20-30 minutes for driver update and a restart of the inference service; with your current cluster size it'll be about 2 hours including health checks and rollbacks if needed. No data is lost — KV cache is ephemeral — but you will see short request failures unless we route traffic to a fallback.

[05:40] Priya: We have a small staging cluster; can you do the upgrade there first? We'll want a runbook.

[06:05] Alex: Absolutely. We'll schedule it for staging first and provide the runbook + rollback steps. We'll also list the exact driver and kernel versions.

[06:30] Samir: One more networking note — our NACLs are pretty restrictive. Some ephemeral ports might be blocked. Could you give a short list of ephemeral ranges you rely on so we can open them temporarily?

[07:00] Jamie: Sure, the important ones are outbound TCP 1024-65535 for ephemeral flows plus 443 for https control plane. If you're using peering, control plane comms go over the peering so it's a bit simpler.

[07:30] Priya: We will validate. Also regarding SSO, Marcus got the SAML metadata last week; we're still working on attribute mapping. Anything Redwood needs from our side for SSO testing?

[07:55] Alex: If you can confirm ACS URL and the NameID format we'll test it. We'll also need a test user with an admin role to validate initial onboarding.

[08:20] Marcus: We'll provide that by tomorrow. Back to the bench — what's the sequence length you recommend for a realistic prod sim?

[08:45] Jamie: For your chat use-case we recommend an 8k sequence test to stress attention kernels and KV cache behavior. Also run a 2k baseline to show delta. We'll test batching at small batch sizes and higher (1, 4, 8) so you can see cost/latency tradeoffs.

[09:15] Priya: Sounds good. How do we measure cost impact for Dedicated vs hosted? We're evaluating long-term whether Redwood Private on our infra or Redwood Dedicated makes more sense.

[09:40] Alex: We'll provide a cost model with token throughput numbers and estimated GPU hours. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and is easier for high sustained usage, Private gives you more control and reduced data plane egress but requires you to handle infra ops and upgrades. We'll attach a simple spreadsheet.

[10:05] Samir: Are there specific kernels or quantization settings we should enable on our nodes? We're running mixed compute currently.

[10:30] Jamie: For best performance with long sequences you want the attention-optimized kernels; we can detect architecture and recommend settings. For quantization, if you need lower memory footprint we recommend 4-bit profiles but that has a small quality delta. We'll share recommended profiles per GPU type.

[11:00] Priya: When you say "detect architecture" is that automatic or part of the install?

[11:20] Jamie: Partly automatic — the Redwood agent reports GPU type and we give a suggested kernel/quantization profile; you can override.

[11:45] Marcus: Ok another compliance question — do you support KMS for model keys? We need encryption at rest for model artifacts.

[12:05] Alex: Yes, Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS/HSM. We'll include the KMS integration steps and required IAM roles.

[12:30] Priya: Great. For the scheduled NAT test, what's the expected data flow? Do we hit the control plane in Redwood or stay entirely peer-to-peer?

[12:50] Jamie: For your current peering setup, inference traffic remains in your VPC and talks to the inference nodes locally; control plane calls (for metrics and management) go over the peering. Egress to external model sources isn't needed for the test.

[13:20] Samir: Minor note — we saw a diff in the logs where the agent referenced "Redwood Console" as "Redwood consoal" in a test export, might be transcript noise.

[13:40] Alex: Ha, those transcripts are fun. Ok, timeline recap: we want bench during NAT open window 2026-09-20 02:00-04:00 UTC; Jamie will run bench and send raw results plus summarized p50/p95/p99 and throughput. We'll also test KV on/off.

[14:10] Priya: We can do that window. Samir will own execution.

[14:30] Samir: Yep. We'll also gather tcpdump snippets if needed.

[15:00] Marcus: About the driver upgrade — is there any chance the upgrade will force a model conversion or anything irreversible?

[15:20] Jamie: No conversion. The runtime uses driver features for newer kernels but models remain unchanged; it's just binary compatibility with CUDA/cuDNN. We'll document exactly which versions are required.

[15:50] Alex: We'll put the upgrade runbook in the Confluence link and share it here. Also listed there are fallback policies — e.g., automatically falling back to a slightly older kernel on restart.

[16:20] Priya: One operational ask — can Redwood provide a small script to validate routes and connectivity (a connectivity check script) we can run before the bench?

[16:45] Jamie: Yes, Jamie: we'll push a small connectivity validator and a sample curl script that hits the local agent endpoints and checks TLS and port connectivity.

[17:10] Priya: Perfect. Also please include a sample iptables snippet for host-level restrictions.

[17:30] Jamie: Will do.

[17:45] Marcus: Anything on the security docs we need to know? Are there extra audits or logs that Redwood keeps?

[18:05] Alex: We retain audit logs configurable by the customer; for Private deployments logs can be pushed to your SIEM via syslog; we'll include the default retention and steps.

[18:30] Priya: Great. On the bench metrics, would you include per-token CPU/GPU utilization? We want to correlate latency spikes with GPU stalls.

[18:50] Jamie: We'll include GPU utilization, memory, CPU and per-process timelines and correlate with token latency. We'll also add a small flamegraph for slow requests.

[19:20] Samir: Can you also include the info about the model catalog versions? We want to pin a model during the POC to avoid drift.

[19:40] Alex: Yes we'll pin a model hash and provide instructions on how to pin in the deployment config.

[20:05] Marcus: Ok let's do a quick recap of owners and dates.

[20:20] Alex: Recap: Jamie runs bench and shares results by 2026-09-21; Jamie provides iptables/examples and connectivity script by 2026-09-18; Alex shares security docs and SOC2 artefacts by 2026-09-17; Priya/Samir to open NAT for 2026-09-20 02:00-04:00 UTC and run test.

[20:55] Priya: Confirmed. Anything else on blockers?

[21:10] Marcus: No from me. Thanks everyone.

[21:25] Alex: Great thanks — we'll follow up in email with attachments and the Confluence link.

[21:40] (crosstalk, meeting closing)

[22:00] End of recording.

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription artifacts and mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash", "consoal").
